## Pull request overview

Introduces a unified **Metadata Plugin Protocol** in `packages/spec` to centralize metadata type registry, querying, lifecycle events, plugin configuration/manifest, and batch/dependency primitives, and expands the `IMetadataService` contract to optionally support these capabilities.

**Changes:**
- Added `kernel/metadata-plugin.zod.ts` defining metadata type registry, query/result, events, validation, config/manifest, bulk ops, and dependency schemas (+ defaults).
- Expanded `contracts/metadata-service.ts` with optional methods for query/bulk/overlay/watch/import-export/validation/type registry/dependencies.
- Added comprehensive test coverage for the new protocol and expanded contract surface.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 5 out of 5 changed files in this pull request and generated 7 comments.

<details>
<summary>Show a summary per file</summary>

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-plugin.zod.ts | New unified metadata plugin protocol schemas + default type registry |
| packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-plugin.test.ts | New tests validating protocol schemas and default registry invariants |
| packages/spec/src/kernel/index.ts | Exports the new metadata-plugin protocol from kernel namespace |
| packages/spec/src/contracts/metadata-service.ts | Expands metadata service contract with optional advanced operations |
| packages/spec/src/contracts/metadata-service.test.ts | Adds tests demonstrating minimal + full-featured contract implementations |
</details>

`MetadataFallbackStrategySchema` is imported but never used. With `noUnusedLocals` enabled in `packages/spec/tsconfig.json`, this will fail type-check/build. Remove the unused import or reference it in the schema as intended.
```suggestion
import { MetadataManagerConfigSchema } from './metadata-loader.zod';
```

The docstring says plugins can extend the metadata type registry via `contributes.kinds`, but `MetadataTypeSchema` is a closed `z.enum(...)`. As a result, schemas that reuse it (e.g. query/events) can't represent custom types. Consider introducing a separate `MetadataTypeIdSchema` (string + constraints) for extensible identifiers, and keep the enum for built-in types only.
```suggestion
 * Metadata Type Identifier
 *
 * Extensible identifier for metadata kinds managed by the platform.
 * - Built-in types are enumerated in {@link MetadataTypeSchema}.
 * - Plugins can contribute additional kinds via `contributes.kinds` in the manifest.
 *
 * Follows the standard machine-name convention (snake_case).
 */
export const MetadataTypeIdSchema = z
  .string()
  .regex(/^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$/, 'metadata type id must be snake_case')
  .describe('Extensible metadata type identifier (built-in + plugin kinds).');

/**
 * Platform Metadata Type Enum
 *
 * Canonical list of built-in metadata types managed by the platform.
 * Each type maps to a specific Zod schema (e.g., ObjectSchema, ViewSchema).
 * For plugin-defined kinds, use {@link MetadataTypeIdSchema}.
```

`MetadataQuerySchema.types` is currently `z.array(MetadataTypeSchema)`, which prevents querying for custom/third-party metadata types (even though `additionalTypes` allows registering them). If custom types are supported, `types` should accept the extensible type identifier schema (e.g. string-based) instead of the closed enum.

`MetadataEventSchema.metadataType` uses `MetadataTypeSchema`, so events can't be emitted for custom metadata types registered via `additionalTypes`/`contributes.kinds`. If extensibility is intended, consider using the same extensible type identifier schema here (and keep the enum for built-ins only).

These default `filePatterns` introduce `*.workflow.ts` / `*.approval.ts`, but OPS naming standards currently only recognize a limited suffix set (see `OPS_FILE_SUFFIX_REGEX` in `kernel/plugin-structure.zod.ts:18`). If tooling relies on OPS suffixes to classify metadata resources, these patterns will be treated as non-standard. Either expand OPS suffix standards to include these new semantic suffixes or align the defaults to the existing suffix scheme.

The default `filePatterns` include `*.permission.ts` / `*.profile.ts` / `*.role.ts`, but OPS naming standards (`kernel/plugin-structure.zod.ts:18`) don't list these suffixes as standard. If the goal is to make this the canonical registry, consider updating OPS suffix standards accordingly (or change the defaults) to avoid inconsistent file discovery/linting behavior.
